open_questions: High-resolution imaging or RV of the 8.4 arcsec neighbour to confirm blend vs on-target variable
dossier.public_summary: This 11-day dip changes depth by more than a factor of 10 between TESS sectors, driven by a couple of unusually deep events, and depth-image centroid is consistent with a nearby star that could mimic the signal. A stable planet transit does not show this sector-to-transit instability and blend, so a false positive is the best explanation.

reasons.why: Depth changes extremely between sectors (5464 ppm in sector 3, 909 ppm in sector 30, 13208 ppm in sector 70; chi2 43.06 dof 2) – a genuine planet should have steady depth.
Tool confirms change is within TESS-SPOC, not a calibration offset between products – real astrophysical depth variation.
Individual transits are inconsistent; 7 of 7 transits, 2 deepest in sector 70 (18328 ppm, 18279 ppm, sigma 4.9, 5.2) carry most signal – signal driven by a few bad/deep events, not a stable transit.

Difference image consistent with target but also with 1 neighbour that could fake it (sep 8.4 arcsec, eclipse_needed 0.0329), and only 1 sector used, so blend cannot be ruled in – supports neighbour/variable origin over planet.
reasons.value: verdict inconclusive offset 9.898 arcsec offset_sigma 2.328, 1 plausible_within_1px

reasons.why: ML planet rank far below median planet (0.5), in the regime where false positives dominate, consistent with depth instability, centroid ambiguity and ~10% planet comparison in similar set.
